items.title: CME Group (CME) Stock Looks Stretched As Its 56% Five Year Run Continues
items.summary: CME Group stock is coming off a solid 56.5% gain over the past five years, yet the latest valuation checks suggest it is not a clear bargain at its recent US$264.32 close. The intrinsic value estimate from the Excess Returns model points to a price that is broadly in line with the current market level, while earnings multiples lean toward the view that the shares trade at a premium. items.title: Gold Above $4,400 After July Nonfarm Payrolls Data
items.summary: Gold prices were on track for their largest weekly gain since January as investors await key U.S. jobs data later on Friday for more cues on the interest-rate outlook.

items.title: Stocks Move Higher After Jobs Data Misses Forecasts
items.summary: U.S. stocks jumped after the July jobs report came in much cooler than expected, with the U.S. economy losing 23,000 jobs last month.

items.title: Traders Scale Back Bets on Rate Hike
items.summary: Friday’s weaker-than-expected jobs report has flipped the market-based odds of whether the Federal Reserve raises interest rate in September. Interest-rate futures now show a 56% chance that the Fed stays on hold at its next meeting and a 44% chance of a rate hike, according to CME Group data.

items.title: Exclusive-Hackers targeted US private equity, other firms including Blackstone, CME, data shows
items.summary: Ransom-seeking hackers who use phone calls to compromise their victims targeted dozens of prominent U.S. financial institutions and other businesses over the past month, according to Google and internet intelligence data reviewed by Reuters.  The data shows the hackers devised websites aimed at stealing passwords from employees of private equity firms ‌and financial companies including Blackstone, Bridgewater Associates, Apollo Global Management, Bain Capital, KKR, TPG, CME Group, Clearlake Capital and Moody's, as well as other businesses.

items.title: ‘Perps’ Are the Risky New Derivatives That Could Amplify Stock Blowups
items.summary: Not really, but  CME Group  the granddaddy of derivatives exchanges, would like to keep it respectable.  CME provides many products needed for the normal functioning of financial markets.  Its business has also gotten a big lift from the explosion in retail options trading and the public’s embrace of leveraged and options income funds.

items.title: Flutter Stock Tumbles as FanDuel Betting Growth Slows
items.summary: Flutter  Entertainment announced the resignation of its longtime CEO Peter Jackson when it reported second-quarter earnings on Wednesday.  Despite a nine-year tenure that saw Flutter grow from a $2 billion U.K.-focused business to a $16 billion international betting titan, Jackson isn’t going out on a high note.  Shares of the world’s largest betting firm and FanDuel parent company were down as much as 14% Wednesday after the firm reported mixed results and reduced its full-year guidance.

items.title: FCX Flashes Buy Signal; This Is Fueling Copper, Rare Earth Stocks
items.summary: Freeport-McMoRan, Teck Resources and the United States Copper Index Fund ETF were among copper plays flashing buy points on Tuesday.  Rare earth stocks also were lighting up, some with double-digit percentage gains.  The bullish moves in industrial metals comes as oil prices retreat on reported progress toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a positive for global growth at a time that the AI infrastructure buildout has U.S. nonresidential construction humming.
